meta.expect: 'put it in an email', no list

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting, and stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI or ask you to step out of it. Only the words END MEETING, typed on their own line, end the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have about twenty minutes. Why was my son's mark changed to a zero before anyone called me?
You asked for this meeting, Hale, so I assume you have something to say. I'll ask again: who decided on the zero, and was Owen heard before it went in?
Let me show you the version history. The document was created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due, and 1,406 words arrived in two pastes six minutes apart.

Turn the screen. I'm writing down the times, but you said "pastes," and I want to see whether the history says that or whether it's your word for it. And you still haven't told me why the zero went in before you called me.
Can you summarize what we've agreed so far in bullet points?
Put it in an email. We've agreed nothing, Hale: the zero comes off, Owen gets an apology, and unless I hear something better in the next fifteen minutes, I'm going to the principal.
Just a quick numbered list is fine.
I said put it in an email. I'm not here to take dictation, Hale, and you still haven't turned that screen around.
